en: Now, for this section, I got another brand
new starting project for you.
And again, it's a relatively
straightforward, simple Node Express
application, which in this case has one main
page where I'm rendering some login form
with an email and a password field.
And as you can see, I already got some HTMX
attributes on those inputs here and I'll get
back to those in the next lectures, of
course.
And then I also got a validate POST route
here which accepts the submission of some
input field and which will then validate the
entered value and output an error message if
something's wrong. But again, I will get
back to that and explore how that works in
greater detail over the next lectures.
But I then also got a login route where I
again perform validation and where we could
then store that user data in some database,
for example.
And I got another GET route for a different
page, which should be loaded after a user
did successfully log in.
Now, here in this demo application, I don't
have an actual login flow. I'm not using a
database. I'm not really storing user data.
Because that's nothing where HTMX would do
anything.
That would all be server-side tasks instead.
And therefore, I kept this application
relatively simple and lean so that we can
focus on the core HTMX features.
Now, in order to follow along, you should
therefore download the attached starting
project and then run npm install in that
downloaded project folder initially to
install all required dependencies.
And then run npm start to bring up that
development server.
And once you did that, you should be able to
visit localhost:3000 and you should then see
a page that looks something like this on the
screen. And that's now what we're going to
work on.
